result.narrative:
Larsen & Toubro scores 28.4, placing it in the Watch band with a PD of 0.1837. The operating picture is strong: Q2 profit rose 33% to Rs 5,202 crore on record order inflows of Rs 147,665 crore, the group won orders worth up to Rs 10,000 crore for the Dhaka Metro project, and three brokers carry Buy ratings. On the payment side there is a single open overdue of 12 DPD under policy TCI-WT-2026-0002, with only one prior overdue on record (resolved 6 days late) and flat accumulation of one notification in each of the last two 6-month windows.

The band is driven almost entirely by news, not by payment behaviour. The trace is 0.65 x 12.0 (payment, 12 DPD) + 0.35 x 58.8 (news) = 28.4: the news component contributes 20.6 points and the payment component only 7.8. The adjudicator agreed with caveats and flagged that without the single severity-3 article the score would be 7.8, which is Healthy, so the Watch placement rests wholly on one source. That source is a report that a Karnataka minister has asked officials to blacklist L&T for delaying works, i.e. a request rather than an executed debarment, and its stored body text is identical to the headline, giving no substantive support for the severity 3 / base 60.0 classification. The adjudicator also noted that the payment notification records owed of INR 83,000,000 while the payment review under the same notification id describes an open overdue invoice of INR 18M; these cannot both be correct.

The recommendation is to maintain the limit at INR 350,000,000 for Trade Credit Insurer under policy TCI-WT-2026-0002, an unchanged exposure, because the PD of 0.1837 sits within the 0.25 appetite target and maximum liability does not bind. Expected loss is 46,292,400 both before and after. Before approving, confirm the correct owed figure and check whether any debarment has actually been issued in Karnataka; the payment agent itself records the trend as insufficient_history, so the 12 DPD should not be read as deterioration.

A return to Healthy needs 8.4 points, which would follow from the overdue clearing and the regulatory item being verified as unfounded or withdrawn. Absent that, the news item decays on a 365-day half-life and currently holds the band on its own, so the score will drift down only slowly. Watch for a confirmed blacklisting or formal debarment, a materially higher owed figure on reconciliation, or the arrears extending toward 38 DPD, which is the payment level that would reach High Risk at 50.0.

judgement.bottom_line: Maintain the INR 350,000,000 limit for Trade Credit Insurer unchanged; PD of 0.1837 is within the 0.25 appetite target and the Watch band reflects news, not payment behaviour. The adjudicator agreed with caveats: the band rests entirely on one unverified severity-3 article (without it the score is 7.8, Healthy), and the owed figure needs reconciling before this goes out.

Reconciliation confirming the lower INR 18M exposure against the 350M limit
